gaps.fact: Tokaji is often bottled in 500 ml bottles, so the glass must be costed from a 500 ml bottle, not a 750.
Many sweet wines are bottled in clear glass; they age for a very long time but must be kept out of direct light.

The Court's line that really old sweet wines become drier over time (perceived sweetness falls as fruit fades and the wine dries on the palate); our copy should say it as perception, not as sugar lost.

A couple of producers in each 1855 Sauternes category for recommending in service: Premier Cru Supérieur Château d'Yquem; Premiers Crus such as Climens, Rieussec, Suduiraut, Coutet, Guiraud; Deuxièmes Crus such as Doisy-Daëne, Filhot, de Malle. The bordeaux article names them, i-626ll87e asks Yquem's class alone, and two Village stems name Rieussec, Suduiraut and Guiraud in passing (c-0tdbku2z on the communes, c-0coqytc6 on their dry whites), but no stem asks the producers by their 1855 category.

Vouvray Moelleux as a noble rot appellation to match with the Loire and Chenin Blanc at Village. Two Régionale Loire stems ask Vouvray's moelleux (i-kc7j7b6f the label term, i-rc8lssjk the cold year that rules it out) and the loire article's label table lists sec, demi-sec, moelleux and doux for Vouvray and Montlouis; but no Village stem matches Vouvray's sweet wine to the Loire and Chenin (c-frthglej asks only its demi-sec sugar against Champagne) and the Sweet Wines chapter names Quarts de Chaume, Bonnezeaux and the Coteaux du Layon without Vouvray.

courtUpdates.now: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1556 (Official Journal, 6 July 2026) approved a revised Tokaj PDO specification: Aszúeszencia, Fordítás Sec and Máslás Sec are abolished, Szamorodni is split into dry and sweet with their own analytical limits, and Aszú stays at 5 or 6 puttonyos with at least 120 g/L of sugar as settled between 2013 and 2024.
courtUpdates.source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1556; The Drinks Business, March 2026; Vinetur, July 2026

courtUpdates.now: The 1855 ranking is unchanged. A draft revision of the Sauternes cahier des charges adopted by the INAO national committee on 27 November 2025 (a new home for the appellation's dry whites, now sold as Bordeaux Blanc) is in the national opposition procedure and not in force.
courtUpdates.source: INAO draft cahier des charges Sauternes, 27 November 2025; Decanter report on the dry white proposal
